newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Portugal set to float up to 49 pct of EDP.
newsitem.headline: Portugal set to float up to 49 pct of EDP.

text.p: The Portuguese government is willing to float up to 49 percent of state electricity concern EDP-Electricidade de Portugal but the actual form of the privatisation will depend on market demand, the country's deputy finance minister said.

"We will try to place as much as possible, depending on market conditions. But even between 20 and 25 percent (EDP) would be the biggest privatisation ever carried out in Portugal," Fernando Teixeira dos Santos told Reuters in an interview.
He said that the privatisation was set, in principle, for May 19 or 20, although it would be the cabinet that fixed the date.
The state company's total worth was more than 1,000 billion escudos ($5.84 billion), Teixeira dos Santos said. But he declined to give a precise figure, saying that it was a matter for ministers.
"If the demand is there, we will place 49 percent...the intention is to be highly flexible," he said.
He said there was no question of seeking a strategic partner for EDP and the shares would be offered on the Lisbon bourse and through a process of bookbuilding both in Portugal and abroad.

"Only further ahead, when we have a clearer idea of the market reaction, particularly internal demand, will we decide on how much for the bourse and how much for direct sale," Teixeira dos Santos said.
